candidates.computation_change_reason: The instream waste concentration columns use a 2.13*Ce multiplier and distinguish acute aquatic, chronic aquatic, human health, domestic supply, irrigation, and livestock/wildlife criteria; interpretation of which column supplies the operative enforceable limit changes compliance results.

Chromium (III), dissolved carries distinct acute (1100.041681) and chronic (143.092822) aquatic criteria while other criteria columns show 1E+100; interpretation of which criterion is enforceable and whether 1E+100 denotes non-applicability affects limit selection.

Chromium (VI), dissolved has different acute (16) and chronic (11) aquatic limits than Chromium (III); whether monitoring and compliance are evaluated against Cr(III), Cr(VI), or total dissolved chromium changes applicable limits and monitoring scope.

A separate Chromium, dissolved row lists 100/100/1000 criteria without species distinction and lacks an MQL value; interpretation of whether this row supersedes or supplements the Cr(III) and Cr(VI) rows changes which numeric limits and monitoring parameters apply.

Two aluminum analyte rows share effluent data but differ in aquatic acute criteria (0 vs 10277.01741) and chronic criteria (10277.0174 vs 4117.35136); the (irr) designation and NMED SOP qualifier affect which analyte, limit, and monitoring requirement apply, and whether a reported result maps to dissolved irrigation aluminum or total recoverable aluminum.

The (P) designation on Antimony, dissolved may signal a conditional or periodic monitoring obligation; interpretation of (P) changes whether monitoring was required for this parameter during Federal FY2025.

Arsenic, dissolved (P) lists both effluent/ambient concentrations and multiple criteria endpoints (human health 9 ug/l, aquatic acute 340, chronic 150); the (P) designation and choice among criteria columns affect both monitoring obligation and which enforceable limit applies.

Cobalt, dissolved has an MQL of 50 but blank ambient and effluent concentration cells alongside zero instream-waste values; interpretation of blank cells as no-discharge, not-required monitoring, or missing evidence changes the established state for no-result cases.

Vanadium, dissolved shows blank Ca/Ce fields with zero instream-waste concentrations; whether blanks represent documented no-discharge, conditional non-requirement, or inadequate evidence affects missing-evidence classification.

Cadmium, dissolved lists hardness-derived acute (3.275645849) and chronic (0.80634471) aquatic limits but blank effluent/ambient cells with zero instream-waste values; interpretation affects both which limit applies when data exist and whether absent results reflect no discharge or unresolved missing evidence.

Total Residual Chlorine lists MQL 33 and aquatic acute (19) and chronic (11) criteria alongside 1E+100 placeholders in other columns; interpretation of which chlorine criterion is operative and whether the parameter is subject to required monitoring affects limit and obligation determinations.

Nitrate and combined nitrite+nitrate rows use mg/l units with different criteria values (10 vs 132); interpretation of which nitrogen parameter is monitored and which criterion applies changes enforceable limits and monitoring obligations.

Radioactivity parameters are expressed in pCi/l with domestic supply (5) and irrigation (30) criteria; unit and endpoint interpretation affects which enforceable limit applies and whether radionuclide monitoring was required.

The sentinel value 1E+100 appears throughout criteria columns; interpretation as a non-operative placeholder versus a numeric criterion determines whether a compliance comparison is applicable for a given parameter and endpoint.
